findings.title: Count errors without sampling metadata as one
findings.body: Allowlisting a project does not backfill sampling metadata into its historical errors, and ordinary errors without a sampling rate can have a null sample_weight. A bare sum(sample_weight) ignores those events, so an allowlisted project's historical or unsampled errors disappear from the reported count; a bucket containing only such errors returns zero. Default missing weights to 1 before summing, and cover mixed sampled and unsampled errors in the integration tests.

findings.title: Require an actual error-only constraint instead of a substring match
findings.body: Both '!event.type:error' and 'event.type:error OR event.type:transaction' contain this substring and therefore enable upsampling when all projects are allowlisted, although neither query restricts results to errors. The endpoint then replaces count() with an error-weight aggregation for non-error events, producing incorrect totals or querying an unsupported field on the transaction dataset. Eligibility must follow the parsed query's constraints, including negation and OR branches.

findings.title: Check eligibility against the dataset actually being queried
findings.body: The eligibility check uses the outer dataset rather than scoped_dataset. For dashboard widgets using the metrics-enhanced Discover-splitting path, the error-only query executes against scoped_dataset=discover while the outer dataset remains a metrics dataset. The helper therefore always rejects upsampling for those error queries, even with allowlisted projects and an explicit event.type:error filter, leaving dashboard counts understated. Use the scoped dataset and effective query when deciding eligibility.

findings.title: Apply upsampling to the top-N selection aggregates too
findings.body: Only timeseries_columns are transformed; selected_columns still contains the request's regular count() aggregate. For a top-events request with field=count() and orderby=-count, the top groups are consequently selected by observed counts while their plotted series use weighted counts. For example, two unsampled events outrank one event with weight 10, excluding the group with the larger reported count. Transform the count aggregate used for top-N selection as well, preserving its ordering alias.
